mainTopic: סוכה תחת סוכה and the gap between the roofs that disqualifies the lower סוכה; a sheet spread over or under the סכך, and decorative sheets.
overview: This עמוד finishes a ברייתא about two סוכות built one above the other. First the גמרא explains when the lower סוכה is כשרה and the upper is פסולה, and when the reverse is true. It answers the challenge פשיטא by showing that the first case teaches there is no גזירה about פסול סכך combining with כשר סכך. Next it asks how much space between the two roofs makes the lower סוכה a סוכה תחת סוכה. רב הונא says one טפח, רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say four, and שמואל says ten. The גמרא challenges שמואל from רבי יהודה in the משנה, and רב דימי answers by reading the משנה as being about a weak lower roof, not about height. A new משנה then teaches that a sheet spread against the sun, against falling leaves, or over a canopy bed makes the area פסולה. רב חסדא limits this ruling: a sheet hung for decoration does not invalidate the סוכה. The גמרא begins bringing a ברייתא about סוכה decorations as support for רב חסדא, and that ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: When the lower sukkah is valid and the upper is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes the case where the lower סוכה is כשרה and the upper סוכה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? The lower סוכה has more shade than sun, the upper סוכה has more sun than shade, and both are within twenty אמות of the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks "what is the case?" and then explains the ברייתא's first scenario, where the lower סוכה is כשרה and the upper one is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper סכך lets in more sun than shade (חמתה מרובה מצלתה), so it is not a real סכך and it cannot turn the lower סוכה into a סוכה תחת סוכה. The lower סוכה has proper shade and is under twenty אמות, so it is כשרה. The upper one fails because it has too little shade.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
The lower (סוכה)
The upper (סוכה)
Its shade is greater than its sunlight, which is the basic requirement for a כשרה סוכה
Twenty אמות, the maximum height for סכך

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the ברייתא's case: a valid סוכה on the bottom with an invalid one built above it.

phrases.english: For example, where the lower one's shade is greater than its sunlight,
and the upper one's sunlight is greater than its shade,
and both of them stand within twenty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? כְּגוֹן שֶׁהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא's first case, which comes from the previous section of the דף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What scenario produces a valid lower סוכה with an invalid upper סוכה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The upper סוכה has more sun than shade, the lower has more shade than sun, and both are under twenty אמות.

steps.title: When the upper sukkah is valid and the lower is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reverse case: the upper סוכה is כשרה and the lower is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes the upper is כשרה and the lower is פסולה. What is the case? Both have more shade than sun, and the upper one is within twenty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's second case and explains when it happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both roofs are real, valid סכך, so the lower סוכה sits under another real סוכה. That makes the lower one a סוכה תחת סוכה, which is פסולה. The upper סוכה is under twenty אמות and has nothing above it, so it is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
Valid
Invalid
Both of them

steps.confusionAlert: The lower סוכה here is perfectly good on its own. It becomes פסולה only because a valid סוכה sits above it.

phrases.english: And sometimes the upper one is valid
and the lower one is invalid
What are the circumstances?
For example, where in both, their shade is greater than their sunlight,
and the upper one stands within twenty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְעָמִים שֶׁהָעֶלְיוֹנָה כְּשֵׁרָה וְתַחְתּוֹנָה פְּסוּלָה הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image case of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What scenario produces a valid upper סוכה with an invalid lower סוכה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both have proper shade and the upper is under twenty אמות, so the lower is a סוכה תחת סוכה.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need for the ברייתא to teach these cases at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that these cases are so simple that the ברייתא did not need to state them. This sets up the next step, which shows what new lesson is hidden here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case follows directly from basic rules: a סוכה needs more shade than sun, it must be under twenty אמות, and a סוכה תחת סוכה is פסולה. So what is the חידוש (new teaching)?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; a challenge asking what new point is being taught

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the necessity of the cases just explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need to list these cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rulings follow directly from known basic rules, so stating them seems pointless.

steps.title: The first case teaches that we make no decree about the roofs combining
steps.stepSummary: The case of a valid lower and invalid upper סוכה was needed to rule out a possible גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a valid lower and invalid upper סוכה was necessary. You might have said: let us decree against it, because perhaps the invalid סכך will combine with the valid סכך. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to the one case that does teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought the חכמים would make a גזירה and disqualify the lower סוכה, since the bad upper סכך might seem to join with the good lower סכך. The ברייתא teaches that there is no such גזירה, and the lower סוכה stays כשרה. The second case really is simple; it is mentioned only to complete the pair.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach)
You might have said
Let us make a rabbinic decree (גזירה)
Combines, joins together
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: A פסול upper roof does not ruin a כשר lower סוכה. There is no גזירה that the two סככים combine.

phrases.english: The case of the lower valid and the upper invalid
was necessary for him.
Lest you say: let us decree
that perhaps the invalid roofing combines
together with the valid roofing,
it teaches us (that we do not).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ. מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden חידוש: the rejection of a possible גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might decree that the lower סוכה is פסולה because the invalid upper סכך could seem to combine with it.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such גזירה exists; the lower סוכה remains כשרה.

steps.title: How much space between the two sukkot makes the lower one invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what distance between the two roofs makes the lower סוכה a separate סוכה תחת סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much space must there be between one סוכה and the other for the lower one to be פסולה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the measurement for סוכה תחת סוכה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two roofs are very close together, they may count as one thick roof, and the lower סוכה would not be disqualified. The גמרא wants the minimum gap that makes the upper one count as a separate סוכה, so that it disqualifies the lower one.

keyTerms.meaning: How much
Between one סוכה and another

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical measurement for when a structure above a סוכה invalidates it.

phrases.english: How much shall there be between one sukkah and the other
for the lower one to be invalid?

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בֵּין סוּכָּה לְסוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case where the lower סוכה is פסולה and asks for its exact measurement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum distance between the two roofs that makes the lower סוכה a סוכה תחת סוכה.

steps.title: רב הונא: one handbreadth, learned from tents of impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that one טפח of space between the roofs is enough. His source is the laws of אהל טומאה, where a space of one טפח counts as a 'tent.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: one טפח, because with tents of טומאה we also find that one טפח counts. As a ברייתא teaches: a space one טפח by one טפח and one טפח high spreads טומאה to whatever is inside it and blocks טומאה from passing beyond it. But if it is less than one טפח high, it does not spread טומאה and does not block it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to the question from Step 5. רב הונא says one טפח is enough, and he proves it from the laws of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of טומאת מת, a covered space one טפח high counts as a real 'tent.' It spreads טומאה inside and blocks it from going out. רב הונא borrows that measure: if one טפח can make a real 'roof' for טומאה, one טפח of space between the two סכך layers makes the lower one a separate סוכה under a roof.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, about 8-10 cm
Tents of ritual impurity, the laws of how a roof spreads or blocks טומאת מת
Brings the impurity: spreads טומאה to everything under the same cover
Blocks the impurity from passing beyond the covering
In height

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about סוכה at all. רב הונא is only borrowing its measurement, the idea that one טפח of space is enough to count as a 'tent.'

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: a handbreadth,
for so we find with tents of impurity: a handbreadth.
(As it was taught:) a handbreadth by a handbreadth, with a height of a handbreadth,
phrases.notes: The minimum size of a space that counts as an 'אהל'.

phrases.english: brings the impurity (to what is under it),
and blocks the impurity (from spreading beyond it).
But less than a handbreadth in height,
does not bring (impurity) and does not block it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: טֶפַח, שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּאׇהֳלֵי טוּמְאָה טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the measurement question asked in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One טפח of space between the roofs is enough, based on the 'tent' measure in the laws of טומאה.

steps.title: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא: four handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says four טפחים are needed, because a space smaller than four is never treated as a significant place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say: four טפחים, because we never find a significant place that is smaller than four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the same question. These אמוראים require four טפחים of space between the roofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They do not compare this to טומאה. They use a general rule: anything under four טפחים is too small to count as a 'place,' as in the laws of domains on שבת. So a gap under four טפחים is not a real space, and the lower סוכה is not considered to be under a separate סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Four (טפחים)
A significant place, a space large enough to count halachically
Less than four טפחים

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי: אַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.english: And Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna say: four,
for we do not find a [significant] place smaller than four.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי: אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רב הונא's to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Four טפחים, the minimum size of a significant place.

steps.title: שמואל: ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a third opinion: the space between the roofs must be ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer. שמואל requires ten טפחים between the two roofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל requires the largest gap of the three opinions. That makes him the most lenient toward the lower סוכה, because it becomes פסולה in the fewest cases. With less than ten טפחים between the roofs, the lower סוכה is not considered to be under another סוכה, and it stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten (טפחים)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question from Step 5.

steps.title: What is שמואל's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל requires ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind שמואל's number. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other two opinions each came with a reason, but שמואל's did not. So the גמרא asks where his ten comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Shmuel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion given in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind שמואל's requirement of ten טפחים.

steps.title: What makes a sukkah valid is what makes another invalid
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's reasoning: a סוכה is only valid if it is ten טפחים tall. So an upper סוכה can only make the lower one invalid if it too has ten טפחים of height.
steps.simpleTranslation: As its validity, so is its invalidity. Just as a סוכה is valid only with ten טפחים, so too it makes something invalid only with ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains שמואל's reason with a matching rule. The same ten-טפחים height needed to make a valid סוכה is needed to create a 'סוכה' that can disqualify the one below it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה below ten טפחים high is not a real סוכה. שמואל reasons that a 'סוכה' over another סוכה only causes a problem if it is a real סוכה, meaning ten טפחים high. With less than that, the upper layer is not a real סוכה and cannot cause the lower one to be 'under a סוכה.'

keyTerms.meaning: Its validity, what makes it a כשרה סוכה
Its invalidity, what makes it disqualify
As... so too: a matching comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions on the gap between roofs: רב הונא says one טפח (from טומאה), רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say four (a significant place), and שמואל says ten (the same height that makes a סוכה valid).

phrases.english: As its validity, so is its invalidity.
Just as its validity is with ten,
so too its invalidity is with ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּהֶכְשֵׁרָהּ כָּךְ פְּסוּלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סוכה needs ten טפחים to be valid, so it needs ten טפחים to make another סוכה invalid.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה to challenge שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in the משנה: if the upper סוכה has no residents, the lower one is valid. This sets up a challenge to שמואל's ten-טפחים rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה says, if there are no residents in the upper סוכה, the lower סוכה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against שמואל by quoting רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. This line is only the setup. The actual argument comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה measures the upper סוכה by whether people can live in it, not by a number like ten טפחים. The גמרא will next define 'residents' and show how this seems to clash with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Residents, people living there
The upper (סוכה)
The lower (סוכה)

phrases.english: We learned (in the mishnah): Rabbi Yehuda says:
If there are no residents in the upper one,
the lower one is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם אֵין דָּיוֹרִין בָּעֶלְיוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts testing שמואל's opinion against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that ten טפחים of space are needed between the roofs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה ties the upper סוכה's effect to whether it can be lived in, not to ten טפחים. The full attack is developed next.

steps.title: What does 'no residents' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה means by 'no residents.' It rejects the literal meaning of actual people living there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'no residents' mean? If you say it means literally no people living there, do people living there really make a difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה's phrase 'אין דיורין' means. It rules out the simple meaning that nobody is actually living in the upper סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a סוכה is valid depends on how it is built, not on whether someone happens to be sitting in it. So 'no residents' cannot simply mean the upper סוכה is empty. The phrase must describe something about the structure itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Residents, people living in a place
If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)
Is that to say? (a rhetorical question showing an idea makes no sense)
They cause it, they make the difference

phrases.english: What does 'there are no residents' mean?
If you say it means actual residents,
Is that to say the residents are what cause it?
phrases.notes: Whether people are living there should not change whether the סוכה is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵין דָּיוֹרִין? אִילֵּימָא דָּיוֹרִין מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out the meaning of the רבי יהודה quote from Step 11 so it can be used against שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of 'אין דיורין' in רבי יהודה's statement.

steps.title: It means a סוכה too short to live in
steps.stepSummary: 'No residents' means the upper סוכה is not fit to live in, which happens when it is less than ten טפחים tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't 'no residents' mean any סוכה that is not fit to be a dwelling? And what is the case? One that is not ten טפחים tall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: 'no residents' means the upper סוכה is not fit to live in. The case is an upper סוכה that is under ten טפחים tall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A space under ten טפחים tall does not count as a dwelling. So רבי יהודה is saying that an upper סוכה under ten tall does not invalidate the lower one. This sets up a direct comparison with שמואל's ten-טפחים rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that (introduces the reading the גמרא prefers)
Fit to serve as a dwelling
And what is the case? (asks for the exact situation)
Ten טפחים tall

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that what 'no residents' means is
any סוכה that is not fit to be a dwelling,
And what is the case?
Where it is not ten טפחים tall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, מַאי אֵין דָּיוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the question asked in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אין דיורין' means an upper סוכה that is not fit to live in because it is under ten טפחים tall.

steps.title: The תנא קמא disagrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה is the one who makes the height distinction, the תנא קמא must hold that the lower סוכה is invalid even when the upper one is under ten. That contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that the תנא קמא holds that even if the upper סוכה is not fit to be a dwelling, the lower one is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יהודה's words that challenges שמואל. If רבי יהודה needed to add this point, the תנא קמא must disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the upper סוכה invalidates the lower one even when it is under ten טפחים tall. שמואל said the upper סוכה only invalidates the lower one if it is ten tall. That makes שמואל follow the minority view of רבי יהודה rather than the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, it follows that
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
Invalid

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge comes from what the תנא קמא implies, not from anything he says outright. We learn his view from the fact that רבי יהודה felt the need to disagree.

phrases.english: By implication, the first tanna holds

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְדִירָה פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: that even if the upper one is not fit to be a dwelling, the lower one is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the meaning set up in Step 13 to complete the challenge against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that ten טפחים are needed for the upper סוכה to invalidate the lower one (Steps 8 and 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה ties validity to a height of ten. So the תנא קמא, who is the majority view, must invalidate the lower סוכה even when the upper one is under ten. That puts שמואל against the majority view.

steps.title: רב דימי: the issue is a weak roof, not height
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a reading from ארץ ישראל: the lower סוכה is valid when its roof cannot hold the upper סוכה's pillows and blankets. On this reading the משנה is not talking about height, so there is no challenge to שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: In ארץ ישראל they say, if the lower סוכה cannot hold the pillows and blankets of the upper one, the lower one is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a different explanation of רבי יהודה from ארץ ישראל. 'No residents' means the lower סוכה's roof is too weak to hold the bedding of anyone living above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, רבי יהודה's point is about how strong the lower סוכה's סכך is, not about how tall the upper סוכה is. If the upper סוכה cannot really be lived in, it does not count as a separate סוכה. Since the משנה is not discussing height at all, it no longer says anything against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (a scholar arriving from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Pillows and blankets
The lower סוכה / the upper סוכה

steps.whyThisMatters: By changing what the argument in the משנה is about, this reading protects שמואל's ten-טפחים rule from the challenge.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said,
they say in the West:
If the lower one is not able
to hold the pillows and blankets of the upper one,
the lower one is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אֲמַר, אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of רבי יהודה that takes away the basis of the challenge in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה: the case is about roof strength, not height.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No residents' means an upper סוכה under ten tall, so the תנא קמא contradicts שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No residents' means the lower roof cannot hold the upper סוכה's bedding. The משנה does not address height, so שמואל stands.

steps.title: Would the תנא קמא invalidate even with a weak roof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב דימי's reading means the תנא קמא invalidates the lower סוכה even when its roof cannot hold the bedding. That would be hard to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that the תנא קמא holds the lower one is invalid even if it cannot hold the bedding?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests רב דימי's reading. It uses the same kind of inference to see what the תנא קמא would then be saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lower roof cannot hold anything, the upper סוכה cannot be lived in at all. It would be strange for the תנא קמא to say such an upper סוכה still invalidates the lower one. So the גמרא needs to find some real difference between the two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: To hold, to bear the weight

phrases.english: Does it follow that the first tanna holds

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְקַבֵּל פְּסוּלָה?
phrases.english: that even if it is not able to hold, the lower one is invalid?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְקַבֵּל פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's reading from Step 15 with the same kind of inference used in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's reading of the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה validates the lower סוכה when its roof cannot hold the bedding, the תנא קמא would seem to invalidate it even then. That makes no sense, because such an upper סוכה cannot be lived in.

steps.title: The argument is about a roof that holds with difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions differ only when the lower roof can hold the bedding, but with difficulty. The תנא קמא says it still counts and the lower סוכה is invalid. רבי יהודה says it does not count and the lower סוכה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is where it can hold the bedding with difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both opinions agree when the roof cannot hold anything at all. They argue only about a roof that holds the bedding with strain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says a roof that holds even with difficulty makes the upper סוכה a real dwelling, so the lower one is invalid. רבי יהודה says a strained roof is not good enough, so the upper סוכה does not count and the lower one is valid. This keeps רב דימי's reading, and with it שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
With difficulty, under strain

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב דימי, the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה argue about a lower roof that holds the upper סוכה's bedding only with difficulty, not about height. So the משנה gives no challenge to שמואל's ten-טפחים rule.

phrases.english: The difference between them is
where it is able to hold the bedding with difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דִּיכוֹלָה לְקַבֵּל עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16 by narrowing the argument to a middle case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the argument to a middle case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא invalidates the lower סוכה even when its roof cannot hold anything.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree that a roof which cannot hold anything leaves the lower סוכה valid. They argue only about a roof that holds with difficulty.

steps.title: The משנה about spreading a sheet in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A sheet above the סכך against the sun, below it against falling leaves, or over a four-post bed canopy makes the area under it פסולה. A sheet over a two-post bed is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone spread a sheet over the סוכה because of the sun, or under the סכך because of falling leaves, or over the frame of a four-post canopy bed, the area is invalid. But he may spread a sheet over a two-post bed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three cases where a sheet makes the סוכה (or the spot under it) invalid, and one case where a sheet is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first two cases the sheet acts as a covering, and a sheet is not valid סכך material. With the four-post bed, the sheet forms a flat roof, so the person sleeps inside a 'tent' and not under the סכך. A two-post bed makes a slanted sheet, which does not count as a real roof, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheet (cloth)
Here it means falling leaves and twigs from the סכך, not an eagle
A four-post bed frame that holds a flat canopy
Two posts, one at each end of the bed, holding a slanted cover
Invalid (the סוכה, or that part of it)

steps.confusionAlert: נֶשֶׁר here does NOT mean 'eagle.' It comes from the word for falling off, and means leaves and bits of סכך dropping down.
steps.whyThisMatters: The exact wording 'because of the falling leaves' becomes the basis of רב חסדא's ruling in the next step.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
If he spread a sheet over it because of the sun
or beneath it because of the falling leaves
or if he spread it over a four-post canopy frame
it is invalid
But he may spread it
over the two posts of a bed
phrases.notes: The cover slants, so it is not a real roof

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ פֵּירַס עָלֶיהָ סָדִין מִפְּנֵי הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier discussion of a סוכה built above another סוכה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sheet above the סכך (against sun), below it (against falling leaves), or over a four-post canopy invalidates. A sheet over a two-post bed does not.

steps.title: A decorative sheet does not invalidate
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה's ruling applies only to a sheet put up to catch falling leaves. A sheet hung to beautify the סוכה leaves it כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב חסדא said: They taught this only when the sheet is there because of the falling leaves. But if it is there to beautify the סוכה, the סוכה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the משנה's second case. A sheet under the סכך only invalidates if it is there to catch falling leaves, not if it is there as decoration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purpose matters. A sheet meant to block falling leaves works as a real covering, so it ruins the סוכה. A decorative sheet is treated as part of the סוכה's beauty, not as a covering, so the סוכה stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught [this law] in the case of...
To beautify it (as decoration)
Valid

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule. Decorative cloths hung under the סכך do not make the סוכה פסולה.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Chisda said
They taught this only when it is because of the falling leaves
but if it is to beautify it, it is valid

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי הַנֶּשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the second case of the משנה in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sheet under the סכך invalidates only when it is put there against falling leaves. A sheet hung for decoration does not invalidate.

steps.title: Isn't רב חסדא's point obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה already says 'because of the falling leaves,' so רב חסדא seems to add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! We learned in the משנה, 'because of the falling leaves'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. The words of the משנה already seem to say what he is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה names the reason as 'falling leaves,' a reader could already conclude that other reasons, like decoration, are different. So why did רב חסדא need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement adds nothing new)

phrases.english: That is obvious!
We learned 'because of the falling leaves'!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא מִפְּנֵי הַנֶּשֶׁר תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב חסדא's statement in step 19 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's statement that a decorative sheet does not invalidate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's own words, 'because of the falling leaves,' already limit the case, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought the משנה just gave the usual case
steps.stepSummary: Without רב חסדא, one might think a decorative sheet also invalidates, and that the משנה said 'falling leaves' only because that is the common reason for a sheet. רב חסדא teaches that the wording is exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the same law applies even to a sheet for beauty, and that the משנה says 'because of the falling leaves' only because that is the usual way things happen. So he teaches us that it is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב חסדא's statement is needed to show that the words 'falling leaves' are a precise condition, not just an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה sometimes describes the typical case without meaning to exclude other cases. רב חסדא tells us this משנה is precise: only a sheet against falling leaves invalidates, and a decorative one does not.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
The usual way things happen (the typical case)
He teaches us [otherwise]

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב חסדא invented a new limit. He is telling us the משנה's wording is exact and not just a common example.
steps.whatToRemember: A sheet under the סכך invalidates only if it is there to catch falling leaves. A decorative sheet does not. The משנה's words are precise.

phrases.english: You might have said
that the same law applies even to beautify it
and the reason it teaches 'because of the falling leaves'
is that it teaches the usual case
So he teaches us otherwise

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ לְנָאוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows that the statement prevents a reasonable mistaken reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה mentions falling leaves only as the typical case, so even a decorative sheet would invalidate.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's wording is exact. Only a sheet against falling leaves invalidates, and a decorative sheet is כשרה.

steps.title: A possible support from a ברייתא about סוכה decorations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports רב חסדא. It describes a properly roofed סוכה decorated with sheets and hanging fruits and foods, and it forbids using those items. It assumes the סוכה stays valid. The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: If he roofed the סוכה properly, and decorated it with colorful curtains and decorated sheets, and hung in it nuts, almonds, peaches and pomegranates, grape clusters and wreaths of grain stalks, wines, oils and flour, it is forbidden to use them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a possible proof for רב חסדא. The ברייתא's quote is not finished yet and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes a properly roofed סוכה decorated with sheets and treats it as a valid סוכה. It forbids using the decorations because they are set aside for the מצוה. If decorative sheets do not invalidate the סוכה, that matches רב חסדא's ruling. The word לֵימָא ('let us say') hints that this proof may later be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say [this source] supports him
He roofed it with סכך according to the law
Colorful embroidered curtains
Clusters (branches) of grapes
To take from them for personal use

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him
If he roofed it properly
and decorated it with colorful curtains
and with decorated sheets
and hung in it nuts, almonds
peaches and pomegranates
clusters of grapes
and wreaths of grain stalks
wines, oils, and fine flour
it is forbidden to take from them for use
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing רב חסדא's ruling, the גמרא looks for a source that supports it.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that a decorative sheet does not invalidate the סוכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing a properly roofed סוכה decorated with sheets and hanging items, treated as a valid סוכה
